Problem numbers refer to the textbook (Chiang & Wainwright, 4th edition). These are not graded, but you should attempt them all before the quiz. Each part has its own **Solution** toggle: try it yourself first, then expand to check.

## Exercise 4.2

**1.** Given
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}7 & -1 \\ 6 & 9\end{bmatrix}, \quad B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 \\ 3 & -2\end{bmatrix}, \quad C=\begin{bmatrix}8 & 3 \\ 6 & 1\end{bmatrix},$$
find:

a. $A+B$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$A+B=\begin{bmatrix}7 & 3 \\ 9 & 7\end{bmatrix}$

</details>

b. $C-A$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$C-A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -8\end{bmatrix}$

</details>

c. $3A$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$3A=\begin{bmatrix}21 & -3 \\ 18 & 27\end{bmatrix}$

</details>

d. $4B+2C$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$4B+2C=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 16 \\ 12 & -8\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}16 & 6 \\ 12 & 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}16 & 22 \\ 24 & -6\end{bmatrix}$

</details>

**2.** Given
$$A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 8 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{bmatrix}, \quad B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 3 & 8\end{bmatrix}, \quad C=\begin{bmatrix}7 & 2 \\ 6 & 3\end{bmatrix}:$$

a. Is $AB$ defined? Calculate $AB$. Can you calculate $BA$? Why?

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$AB$ is defined, since the number of columns in $A$ is two, which equals the number of rows in $B$.
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}
2 \times 2+8 \times 3 & 2 \times 0+8 \times 8 \\
3 \times 2+0 \times 3 & 3 \times 0+0 \times 8 \\
5 \times 2+1 \times 3 & 5 \times 0+1 \times 8
\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}
28 & 64 \\
6 & 0 \\
13 & 8
\end{bmatrix}$$

Not possible to calculate $BA$: $B$ has two columns, but $A$ has three rows.

</details>

b. Is $BC$ defined? Calculate $BC$. Is $CB$ defined? If so, calculate $CB$. Is it true that $BC=CB$?

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$BC$ and $CB$ are both defined, as both are $2 \times 2$.
$$BC=\begin{bmatrix}
14 & 4 \\
69 & 30
\end{bmatrix} \neq CB=\begin{bmatrix}
20 & 16 \\
21 & 24
\end{bmatrix}$$

</details>

**4.** Find the product matrices in the following (in each case, append beneath every matrix a dimension indicator):

a. $\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}8 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 5\end{bmatrix}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 36 & 20 \\ 16 & 3\end{bmatrix}_{3 \times 2}$

</details>

b. $\begin{bmatrix}6 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -1 \\ 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$\begin{bmatrix}49 & 3 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}_{2 \times 2}$

</details>

c. $\begin{bmatrix}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 4 & 2 & -7\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$\begin{bmatrix}3x+5y \\ 4x+2y-7z\end{bmatrix}_{2 \times 1}$

</details>

d. $\begin{bmatrix}a & b & c\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$\begin{bmatrix}7a+c & 2b+4c\end{bmatrix}_{1 \times 2}$

</details>
